title: The Forms of Shiva and Vishnu
translation: With the noose, goad, snake, damaru drum, skull-cup, trident, skull-staff, spear, arrow and bow, ten objects held in his hands and exchanged from hand to hand, how many different forms of Shambhu (Shiva) are there? And likewise of Hari (Vishnu), with the four: mace, discus, lotus and conch?
translation_hi: पाश, अंकुश, सर्प, डमरू, कपाल, त्रिशूल, खट्वांग, शक्ति, बाण और धनुष, इन दस वस्तुओं को अलग अलग हाथों में बदल बदल कर रखने से शंभु (शिव) के कितने रूप बनते हैं? और इसी प्रकार गदा, चक्र, कमल और शंख से हरि (विष्णु) के कितने रूप बनते हैं?
question: How many different forms of Vishnu are there?
solution:
The first hand can hold any of the 4 objects, the second any of the 3 left, then 2, then 1:

4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 4! = 24 forms of Vishnu

For Shiva's ten objects: 10! = 10 × 9 × … × 1 = 3,628,800 forms

Science link: this is the factorial, n!, the number of ways to arrange n things. In the Lilavati it comes from the अङ्कपाश (ankapasha) chapter on permutations. In your puja: the 24 names recited during achamana and sandhya (केशव, नारायण, माधव, गोविन्द…) are traditionally the 24 forms of Vishnu, each told apart by the order of shankha, cakra, gada and padma in his four hands. Exactly 4! = 24.
